methods.label: Coherence
methods.say: Magnitude-squared coherence, mean over the band. Blind to delay; sees volume conduction.

methods.label: Imaginary coherence
methods.say: |imaginary part of coherency|, mean over the band. Zero for anything at zero lag.

methods.label: Raw cc
methods.say: Peak r of the band-passed traces within two cycles (signed).

methods.label: Envelope cc
methods.say: Peak r of the band's envelopes within two cycles (signed).

methods.label: Amplitude r, zero lag
methods.say: Pearson r of the two envelopes at zero lag.

methods.label: Orthogonalised envelope r
methods.say: Envelope r after removing each signal's zero-lag share of the other (Hipp 2012).

methods.label: PPC
methods.say: Pairwise phase consistency: PLV without its sample-size bias.

methods.label: PLI
methods.say: Phase-lag index: how consistently one leads.

methods.label: Granger A→B
methods.say: Spectral Granger causality, first region to second (nats).

methods.label: Granger B→A
methods.say: Spectral Granger causality, second region to first (nats).

methods.label: Granger net
methods.say: A→B minus B→A: positive means the first region drives the second more.

name: Monolith · Precon1→4 · 1–55 Hz
points_rule: p < 0.05 (uncorrected), most rats the same way first, then p; at most 3 per region pair; within 2 Hz in the same window and method is the same finding

why.1: fewer than 5 rats have it on both days
why.2: a rat had a single usable value on a day, so there is no spread to put an error on
why.3: a rat gave the identical value in every cue pair
why.4: every rat changed by exactly the same amount
why.5: no rat has it on both days
